https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm0e.text: Image source, EPA Image caption, Trump announced the ban on Friday, accusing the organisations of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration By Alicia Curry Â and Â Bernd Debusmann ,Â White House reporter Published 21 September 2026, 11:57 BST Updated 1 hour ago CNN, Politico and MS NOW have sued the Trump administration after the three US media outlets were barred from the White House. President Donald Trump announced the ban on Friday, accusing the organisations of writing "fiction or lies" about his team. The companies said their reporters were denied access to the building on Saturday. In a joint statement on Monday, they said they were pursuing legal action to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports". Major US TV networks later announced they would suspend their White House pooled coverage of Trump, leaving a potential gap as he heads to New York for the United Nations General Assembly. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, A journalist from MS NOW broadcasts from a street corner outside the White House grounds The First Amendment forbids the government from "abridging" the freedom of the press - language that courts have traditionally interpreted as preventing the government from discriminating against the media based on the content of their coverage. The statement from CNN, Politico and MS NOW said: "Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting. "Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference." The media organisations filed the lawsuit on Monday in US District Court in Washington, asking a judge to quickly rule Trump's ban unconstitutional and prevent his aides from enforcing it. Earlier, in a posting on Truth Social, Trump said the White House was not "instituting an assault on the Free Press" and that he was targeting "FAKE NEWS". On Monday morning, major US TV networks pulled out of White House pool duties, which sees media organisations share material with each other to save on costs and space when broadcasting presidential events to the American public. Fox News Washington bureau chief Bryan Boughton, who currently holds a rotating role helping to organise media TV crews covering the White House, wrote in an email seen by the BBC that "effective today, the TV pool will not be covering designated as pool coverage" of President Trump. The message said the move followed the White House "preventing" CNN from fulfilling its pool duties for Trump's trip to New York and that "there will be no replacement pool put in place". CNN - one of only five US news outlets in the White House press pool for live television - was originally due to cover Trump's trip to the UN General Assembly in New York on Monday and Tuesday. But on Monday morning, the five-seat CNN booth in the basement of the White House press area - typically manned throughout the day from the early hours of the morning - was empty and closed. Screens and monitors inside were turned off. Instead, a CNN crew was outside the secured area of the White House grounds, broadcasting live from a public pavement. Five TV networks, ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC, issued a joint statement: "The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. "No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting." Those five networks are considered the only ones with the money and infrastructure to distribute live coverage from the White House and presidential events. For now, the White House media slot has remained vacant and instead the conservative TV outlet, Real America's Voice, was listed as "secondary" crew on Trump's trip to New York, where he will meet Mayor Zohran Mamdani and French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Empty broadcast booths on the White House grounds after journalists from three media organisations were denied entry Announcing his ban on CNN, Politico and MS NOW last week, Trump did not mention specific stories or reporting that prompted the move, but later said "it's really just cumulative stories over the last few years". The US president added that there "may be others to join them". When later asked by a reporter what he meant by this, Trump responded: "Others to come in terms of fake news? Well, you know, the New York Times is fake news, the Washington Post is fake news." In February, the White House announced it was taking control of the press pool which has access to Trump and had for more than a century been managed by the White House Correspondents' Association. The same month, the administration moved to bar Associated Press (AP) reporters and photographers from spaces where access is limited, such as the Oval Office or Air Force One, because of the outlet's usage of the term "Gulf of Mexico" instead of "Gulf of America". AP filed a lawsuit and the case remains ongoing. There have been a few instances of other administrations attempting to limit certain outlets' access. The Obama administration tried to exclude Fox News from participating in a press pool interview with an administration official in 2009. But after pushback from the other four networks in the pool, Fox News was granted access. But unlike with Trump's exclusion of CNN, MS Now and Politico, the Obama administration did not try to bar Fox News from all pool coverage, just one specific interview. Trump has been frequently critical of news organisations and his administration has launched legal action against a series of outlets, including the New York Times, the Wall Street Journal and the BBC. Some of the lawsuits have resulted in media organisations agreeing to pay multimillion dollar settlements. Trump's lawsuit against the BBC is ongoing. Skip next section UAE honors Indian Captain Smit Machchhar over Dubai-Tel Aviv flight attack 10/28/2026 October 28, 2026 UAE honors Indian Captain Smit Machchhar over Dubai-Tel Aviv flight attack UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II on Indian Captain Smit Machchhar and his crew members, in recognition of their courage during an attempted mid-air attack in September. A Flydubai flight was headed from Dubai to Tel Aviv when violence broke out in the cockpit. The co-pilot reportedly stabbed the captain in an apparent attempt to crash the plane, which was carrying 174 passengers — mainly Israeli nationals. Despite his severe injuries, Machchhar opened the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the co-pilot. An off-duty crew member reportedly took control and made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The UAE described the incident as a "terrorist attack." Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Dubai’s crown prince and the UAE’s deputy prime minister and defense minister, presented the medals and praised the crew’s courage and sense of responsibility, the Dubai Media Office said. The storm lost some speed after a prolonged lanfall, downgrading it to a "severe cyclonic storm" from a "very severe cyclonic storm." It is expected to further weaken into a "cyclonic storm" and turn into a "deep depression" by the evening, National Disaster Response Force Inspector General (IG) Narendra Singh Bundela told reporters in New Delhi. "North of Andhra Pradesh and the southern part of Odisha have been the most affected due to Cyclone Arnab. Strong winds and rainfall are being witnessed in a few districts of the two states," Bundela said. "Andhra Pradesh has been the most affected... we have been informed that trees have been uprooted, 31 houses of various types have been damaged and three persons have been killed," he said, adding that the impact on Odisha was not serious as per preliminary reports. The IG said nearly 40 NDRF teams had been deployed to regions along India's east coast to manage the impact of the cyclone. https://p.dw.com/p/5OlP8 Skip next section India faces high economic cost of heatwaves, new Lancet study shows 10/28/2026 October 28, 2026 India faces high economic cost of heatwaves, new Lancet study shows Half of the heatwave days that people in India were exposed to on average were directly attributable to climate change between 2016 and 2025 Image: Debarchan Chatterjee/NurPhoto/IMAGO India ranked among the top countries where the elderly and infants are most exposed to heatwaves, the latest Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change report said, putting the nation in the same basket as China, US and Russia. But that's not all. As per the report, the economic cost is steep for the nation. Extreme heat cost Indian workers an estimated $174 billion (€156.5 billion) in potential earnings in 2025. That's 4.2% of the nation's GDP. Moreover, 54% of the losses were from the agriculture sector. "Increasing heat exposure is affecting health, physical activity, sleep and labor capacity in India, with substantial consequences for livelihoods, particularly in agriculture," the report said. Published by the presitigious British medical journal ahead of the COP 31 climate summit in November, the 10th edition of the report brought together 146 researchers from 30 countries to assess the impact of climate change on the health of the world's population. It said there were a record 710,000 heat-related deaths in 2023 with more than 70% of that toll linked to human-caused climate change. The report called for climate change to be formally recognized and addressed as a global health emergency. https://p.dw.com/p/5OlAz Skip next section Jio Platforms becomes second-most valuable firm on stock market debut 10/28/2026 October 28, 2026 Jio Platforms becomes second-most valuable firm on stock market debut Shares of Jio Platforms, a Reliance Industries-backed digital services company owned by India's richest man, Mukesh Ambani, listed on the India stock exchanges with a premium of over 21%. That instantly made the company the second most valuable on the exchanges. Jio's telecommunications business serves over 530 million customers and is backed by Meta Platforms ​and Alphabet's Google. Its user numbers are second only to China Mobile on the basis of ​single-country subscribers. The listing, the first for the Reliance conglomerate in two decades, ​furthers Ambani's ‌plan to turn Reliance from an oil-and-chemicals conglomerate into an "everything company" spanning consumer products and technology. This was the first public listing for the Reliance conglomerate in two decades Image: Indranil Mukherjee/AFP The listing was attended by the Ambani family, that is Mukesh Ambani himself, his wife Nita, eldest son Akash and other children Isha and Anant. Meanwhile, major Indian newspapers on Wednesday carried front-page ads from Reliance Jio, ⁠saying "Thank you, India." Visuals on social media, from overnight and today morning, show high winds and storm surges. Heavy rainfall flew vertically as old trees struggled to stay upright. Many failed. Local news agencies ANI and PTI showed heavy rainfall and unruly sea water smash the coast of India's southern state, Kerala. Other footage circulating on social media showed lanes full of fallen trees and broken power lines. Other showed violent winds and heaping waves spill on to a coastal street. These videos were posted by general users and remain unverified. Old videos of other storms tend to circulate on various channels in such situations. Users are best adviced to remain skeptical and take information provided by verified or government sources. https://p.dw.com/p/5Ol5e Skip next section Cyclone Arnab batters Andhra Pradesh with drawn-out landfall 10/28/2026 October 28, 2026 Cyclone Arnab batters Andhra Pradesh with drawn-out landfall "Very severe" Cyclone Arnab made a sooner-than-expected landfall along India's east coast and is now "practically stationary" at the edge, authorities said. The storm, with winds over 125 kilometers per hour (78 miles per hour) and gusts of 150 kilometers per hour (93 miles per hour), is in the third-highest category of storms on a scale of five. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) said its landfall would last for over two hours and that the edge of the storm was already on the coast of the south-eastern state of Andhra Pradesh. Its center remains over sea. This is a satellite view of Cyclone Arnab making landfall on the east coast of India Image: CSU/CIRA & EUMETSAT/REUTERS Power, transport disrupted The cyclone brought heavy rains, high winds and disruption to Andhra and its neighboring state of Odisha. Gales rocked trees, winds and heavy rain disrupted power lines and the storm caused the sea to surge like many locals had never seen before. Flight and train services were also impacted. "There was a cyclone here three years ago, but the water didn't rise this much," a 35-year-old local resident said, adding that the government had warned them to stock up on groceries beforehand. The weather agency warned of "total destruction" of thatched houses, localized flooding, the uprooting of power and communications poles, and "widespread damage" to standing crops. No casualties so far No loss of life has been reported in either states as of Wednesday morning. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu credited advance precautionary measures for preventing casualties so far. He said so during a teleconference meeting to monitor the impact of the storm onground, news agency Press Trust of India reported. Together, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha evacuated nearly 100,000 people from vulnerable regions in preperation of the storm. They were moved inland fro better shelter. Thousands of people from coastal, low-lying regions have been moved inland Image: Noah Seelam/AFP "Our homes get flooded, and we have to stay in the water," said Rajeshwari, 65, who gave only one name and had been taken to a government-run shelter near Kakinada. "So the government provided us with a bus, and we came here to shelter," she told AFP. In Nepal, authorities warned tourists against ​venturing into high-altitude areas ‌due to fears that Arnab could trigger torrential downpours, snowstorms and avalanches in the Himalayan region from Thursday night ​through Saturday. Arnab formed on Monday morning in the Bay of Bengal, a region known for birthing some of the deadliest storms to batter India. This year's season, however, is turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon which is causing unprecedented warming , experts say. What happens when El Nino meets climate change? https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvze.text: Image source, Getty Images By Jaroslav Lukiv Published 4 hours ago The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the issue. The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks. The BBC contacted the FBI for comment. This comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors in the US last week. Officials have said they were not caused by cyberattacks, but the blackouts have sparked scrutiny from lawmakers. White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week, with US President Donald Trump saying he was not good enough. It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US. In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber-crime group ShinyHunters, which claimed it had stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff - around 38,000 people. After that hack, one former FBI agent told the BBC he feared for the safety of current employees, whose personal information could soon become available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers. In a separate development, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) . Employees were informed on Thursday that its farm payment system had been targeted, NBC said. The USDA has not publicly commented on the issue. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqy7.text: Figure caption, Huge fire erupts near Cairo killing at least 30 people By Aleks Phillips Published 25 November 2026 Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says. Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening. Footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched. Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol. The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead. The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation. It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says. Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital. Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished, as emergency services blocked off entry routes. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Images from the scene show a large crowd gathered on the highway after the fire had been extinguished Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The tanker crossed the highway's central reservation before overturning and bursting into flames, local media report The health ministry said 39 ambulances had been dispatched to respond to the fire, while it posted images of Egypt's health minister overseeing the treatment of the injured at one of Cairo's hospitals. Road collisions are also common in Egypt, often attributed to lax maintenance and the widespread flouting of traffic laws. Nearly 6,000 people died on Egypt's roads last year, official figures show, a rise of several hundred on the previous year's total. Emergency responders have since cleared the highway and allowed it to reopen, state broadcaster NMA reports. A bulldozer could earlier be seen at the scene clearing the burnt-out wrecks of cars.
